content.text: {"headline":"Approve P2: move 6 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 15:30-16:00 and delay payments breaks by 30 min, at no extra cost.","why":"The card authorisation gateway outage (P1 incident from 12:37) is driving extra payments calls. card_declined calls are at 2.48x normal, and the 12:30 interval took 240 calls against 108 forecast. Staffing is only 3-4 agents below plan, so this is a demand problem, not an absence problem. For the 15:30-17:30 window, P2 predicts 100.0% service level overall, with payments at 100.0%, general at 100.0% and 0.0% abandons, against an 80% target. Rest of day rises to 97.2%. It costs nothing and breaks no policy.","trade_offs":["Doing nothing (P0) or the smaller 4-agent move (P1) is also forecast to clear target at 99.4%, with payments at 99.0%. P2 adds a little extra margin in case the outage surge persists, for the price of 2 more agents moved and a short break delay.","P3 moves 8 agents and delays general breaks too, but predicts slightly less (99.9%, rest of day 96.6%). It puts more strain on general for no gain.","General is predicted to stay at 100.0% under P2, so the risk to the other queue looks low. All options are no-cost."],"watch":"Watch payments call volume and card_declined calls through 15:30-16:00, and check for updates on the gateway incident. If the outage worsens or volumes climb well above the current surge, reassess. Make sure the delayed payments breaks are given once the peak passes. No escalation is needed."}
